title: Random Forest
description: Ensemble learning method based on bagging of randomized decision trees.
name: Random Forest
summary: Random Forest constructs a multitude of decision trees at training time and outputs the class that is the mode of the classes (classification) or mean prediction (regression) of the individual trees, reducing variance via bootstrap aggregating (bagging).
use_when: Building a robust tabular classifier or regressor with default hyperparameters and minimal tuning.
avoid_when: Executing predictions in ultra-low latency setups where trees are too slow to evaluate.
pros: Highly resistant to overfitting due to bagging and feature randomization.
Native computation of feature importances for explainability.
Requires very little hyperparameter tuning to achieve high performance.
cons: Can be slow to execute at inference time when ensemble size is large.
Large memory footprint when storing hundreds of deep decision trees.
Cannot extrapolate beyond the range of training values in regression.

key_hyperparams.name: n_estimators
key_hyperparams.note: The number of trees in the forest. Generally, more trees improve accuracy but slow down training/inference.

quick_start:
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
import numpy as np

X = np.random.randn(100, 4)
y = np.random.randint(0, 2, size=100)
clf = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100).fit(X, y)
preds = clf.predict([[0, 0, 0, 0]])
